desk.headline: Distributable earnings per share up 8.6% to 62.17c, ahead of 7–8% guidance; dividend 55.96c; FY27 guided at 8–10% growth
results: Distributable earnings per share rose 8.6% to 62.17c, beating the 7–8% growth the company had guided; total distributable earnings rose 22% to R636m as new shares were issued.
Total dividend for the year rose to 55.96c from 51.53c, a 90% payout; shareholders can reinvest the 28.45c final dividend in new shares.
Revenue excluding straight-lining rose 11%, as reported; headline earnings per share rose about 20% to 63.86c.
Vacancy fell to 6% from 8.5% (retail 4.5%, offices 21.7%) and tenant retention improved to 85% from 76%.
Dipula bought 14 properties worth R3bn, including nine Moolman shopping centres for R2bn, and gearing eased to 31.8% with interest cover at 3.2x.

guidance.summary: Dipula expects distributable earnings per share to grow 8–10% in FY2027, after delivering 8.6% in FY2026 against guidance of 7–8%.

points: CEO Izak Petersen called it a transformative year, pointing to careful capital management, selective buying and redevelopment.
He said there is a good pipeline of further deals and Dipula will keep looking at acquisitions.
Management is shifting the mix towards retail and industrial; retail should be close to 80% of income after the Moolman deal and offices below 10% soon.
Petersen sees retail potential in underserved regions such as Limpopo, while Gauteng is nearing saturation.
After year-end Dipula agreed to sell most of its non-core residential properties for R268m and plans about R250m of further capex over 12–18 months.
call.source: The National (11 Nov 2026), Catchwords/Bizcommunity (12 Nov 2026) and Business Explainer (12 Nov 2026) coverage of the results

watch: Transfer of the nine Moolman shopping centres from late November 2026 and how quickly they add to earnings.
Progress toward the 8–10% FY2027 distributable earnings growth guidance at the interim stage.
Office vacancy, still above 20%, and the R268m residential disposal.
